issues_detected.description: No software_and_tools slot anywhere in the record. The format-conversion tooling that preprocessing_strategies describes (Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt to DICOM, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, ECG to WFDB) is unnamed and unversioned, and the 'additional processing steps' the central project team performed before dissemination are not attributed to any named tool. Only REDCap, the MoCA Duo application and the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard are named in passing inside other slots, and the AI-READI GitHub organization is given as a bare organization URL with no repository named
issues_detected.recommendation: Add software_and_tools entries naming the conversion and curation tools with versions and the specific repositories under https://github.com/AI-READI, and link the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard tool with its version

issues_detected.description: sensitive_elements carries two entries whose booleans contradict each other: entry 0 has sensitive_elements_present false (healthsheet reading, public release) and entry 1 has sensitive_elements_present true (RO-Crate rai:personalSensitiveInformation). A consumer reading the boolean alone gets opposite answers. The record explains in source_caveats on both entries that the two sources enumerate different things (sensitive attributes vs data-source categories) and states which reading governs, but the structured booleans remain in conflict
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep one entry carrying the governing boolean for the released data and demote the RO-Crate data-source list to a note or a differently-typed slot, so the boolean is unambiguous

issues_detected.description: Institutional attribution is unreconciled across three slots: data_governance.accountable_organization is Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) following FAIRhub study metadata, while ethical_reviews[0] and human_subject_research.ethics_review_board place the IRB at the University of Washington Human Subjects Division (protocol STUDY00016228, hsdrely@uw.edu), and funders records award OT2OD032644 with the University of Washington as awardee organization. The record flags this at the record root and on both slots rather than resolving it
issues_detected.recommendation: State which institution the record treats as authoritative for governance as distinct from IRB oversight, and keep the other as a recorded alternative

issues_detected.description: No data_protection_impacts slot is present at all. With human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects true, regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted' and an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk, the absence of even a negative statement ('no DPIA was conducted') leaves the question unanswered rather than answered in the negative
issues_detected.recommendation: Add data_protection_impacts, stating explicitly that no data protection impact assessment was conducted if that is what the bundle supports

issues_detected.description: The variables list ends with an entry named 'Representative subset marker' with data_type string, which is a scope note rather than a variable in the dataset. Its own quality_notes says so. A consumer counting variables or generating a data dictionary from this slot picks up a non-variable row
issues_detected.recommendation: Move the scope statement into a record-level note on the variables slot and remove the pseudo-variable entry

issues_detected.description: Two related_datasets entries put journal-article DOIs (doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449) in target_dataset under relationship_type is_described_by. Each description states plainly that the target is an article rather than a dataset, so the deviation is disclosed, but the slot is dataset-typed
issues_detected.recommendation: Carry the describing publications in a citation or external_resources slot and reserve related_datasets for dataset targets

issues_detected.description: The inner external_resources lists hold long prose paragraphs with URLs embedded in them rather than URL strings, which is what the slot description specifies for the ExternalResource class. Every URL that appears is well formed and on a plausible domain (docs.aireadi.org, aireadi.org, zenodo.org, github.com, cds-specification.readthedocs.io)
issues_detected.recommendation: Split each entry into its URLs in the inner list and move the surrounding prose into the entry's description or notes

issues_detected.description: No conflict-of-interest declaration appears anywhere, and no patent or commercialisation statement. In-kind device loans from Topcon, Optomed, iCare World and Carl Zeiss and research discounts from Heidelberg Engineering, Dexcom and Garmin are recorded under funders, and those same devices are the measurement instruments, so the disclosure exists as funding information but is never framed as a conflict of interest
issues_detected.recommendation: Add an explicit conflict-of-interest statement to ethical_reviews covering the device manufacturer in-kind contributions and any patent or commercialisation position

issues_detected.description: No variable carries an ontology or dictionary identifier (no LOINC, no OMOP concept id, no variable id), and no character encoding is stated for any distributed format. The nine variables are a self-declared representative subset of an inventory that includes roughly forty laboratory analytes plus questionnaire, imaging, waveform, wearable and environmental variables
issues_detected.recommendation: Add identifiers to the variables that have them (LOINC for laboratory analytes, OMOP concept ids for the clinical tables) and state the character encoding of the CSV, JSON and Markdown distributions

semantic_insights: The identifier chain is internally consistent: DOI prefix 10.60775 is FAIRhub's, publisher is https://fairhub.io/, page is https://fairhub.io/datasets/3, and version_access.latest_version_doi (doi:10.60775/fairhub.3) matches the record id, the doi slot and version 3.0.0

Both arithmetic caveats the record raises are verifiable from the record's own file_collections: the nine directory file counts sum to 356,334, exactly nine short of total_file_count 356,343, and the record names the nine root metadata files that account for the difference; the nine directory sizes sum to 3,815,969,360,064, exactly the 419,614-byte shortfall against total_size_bytes 3,815,969,779,678 that the caveat states
The recommended split arithmetic is fully consistent: 1,576 + 352 + 352 = 2,280, and each per-split race/ethnicity, sex and diabetes-status breakdown sums to its own split size
Cohort aggregates in subpopulations.distribution sum to 2,280 on all three axes (race/ethnicity 380+545+519+836; sex 951+1,329; diabetes status 776+560+686+258), matching instances[0].counts

Grant OT2OD032644 follows the NIH pattern (activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032644); the record additionally gives the full application form 1OT2OD032644-01, application id 10471118, award amount and project period, and the well-formed supplementary awards P30DK035816 and UL1TR003096

HIPAA Safe Harbor is an appropriate de-identification method for this health data type, and the record reconciles FAIRhub's 'NoDeIdentification' type code with the Safe Harbor account by explaining that no identifiers were collected in the first place, rather than leaving two bare contradictory claims

Two derived values are labelled as derived rather than passed off as quoted: confidentiality_level 'restricted' and hipaa_compliant 'compliant' each carry a source_caveat saying no source in the bundle uses those words, and the RO-Crate's own unmappable term 'HL7:2N (normal)' is preserved in prose

Temporal ordering holds throughout: collection 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01, release 2025-11-17, with v1.0.0 (2024-05-03), v2.0.0 (2024-11-08) and v3.0.0 (2025-11-17) in order and each tied to its own DOI and participant count
ClinicalTrials.gov registration NCT06002048 is well formed, and the study is recorded as not FDA-regulated with no data monitoring committee, consistent with an observational cohort

known_biases uses four distinct BiasTypeEnum values (selection, sampling, representation, measurement) with mitigation strategies for each, and representation_bias additionally names affected_subsets, which is the structured RAI-aligned form the sub-element asks for
is_tabular false is consistent with the composition described: imaging in DICOM, waveforms in WFDB, wearable data in Open mHealth and only the clinical directory in tabular OMOP CDM form

The record states an explicit negative on labelling (instances[0].label false, description says no annotation or labeling was performed so the release stays hypothesis-agnostic), which answers the labelling question rather than leaving it blank

correctness_validations.url_validity: all URLs well formed and on plausible domains; inner external_resources entries are prose containing URLs rather than URL strings

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; per-version DOIs 10.60775/fairhub.1 and 10.60775/fairhub.2
sub_elements.quality_note: DOI matches the 10.XXXXX/ pattern and the 10.60775 prefix is FAIRhub's, consistent with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and the /datasets/3 landing page. Per-version DOIs are carried for all three releases. No RRID is present, which the sub-element does not require given a valid DOI.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title/name: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description is roughly 2,300 characters naming 2,280 participants, three sites, the 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window, every modality with its format standard, 356,343 files at 3.82 TB, the CDS v0.1.1 layout, the absence of labels and what the public release omits
sub_elements.quality_note: Well beyond the 200-character bar and specific throughout: counts, dates, sites, formats and the public/controlled split are all in the description rather than deferred.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam, Data Sharing, Exploratory Data Collection
sub_elements.quality_note: Nine keywords spanning condition, methods and modalities, above the five-keyword bar and non-generic.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; file_collections lists nine datatype directories each with id, name, path, collection_type, file_count, total_bytes, description and conforms_to_standard; subsets lists the public, controlled-access and mini-subset releases
sub_elements.quality_note: Landing page resolves on the named platform and the hierarchical structure is unusually complete, with per-directory counts and sizes that reconcile against the dataset totals.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1; is_described_by doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449; subsets records the mini-subset as FAIRhub child dataset id 4
sub_elements.quality_note: Four typed relationships with resolvable DOI targets and per-target descriptions. Two of the four point at journal articles rather than datasets, which the record discloses in each description.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license: AI-READI custom license v2.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms describes the Data License Agreement v2.0 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036) with storage restrictions, BAA requirements, derivative and synthetic data treatment, acknowledgement obligations and automatic termination on breach; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research; ip_restrictions.restrictions reserves title and all IP to the Licensor
sub_elements.quality_note: Access policy and IP position are both stated in operative terms, not by reference. The record also names the three different labels the bundle uses for the same license and says which was chosen for the scalar slot.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions list covers NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security best practices and watermarking obligations; other_compliance records not FDA-regulated and Safe Harbor de-identification; notes preserve the RO-Crate's unmappable 'HL7:2N (normal)'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both scalar values carry a source_caveat stating they are derived from the described access model and the FAIRhub/Nature Metabolism statements, because no source uses those words. That is the right treatment for a derived enum value.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[0].access_urls: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 and https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access; data_governance.access_review_process records 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' and the verified-ID login, disease-specific use attestation and license agreement; version 3.0.0 documentation adds Azure Storage access guidance
sub_elements.quality_note: No download_url scalar, but the platform links and the access procedure are both explicit, which is what the sub-element asks for. The controlled-access route via data use agreement is stated separately.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: FAIRhub platform download with self-attestation; mini-subset for pipeline development; DICOM (application/dicom); CSV (text/csv); JSON (application/json); Markdown (text/markdown). Per-directory conforms_to_standard adds WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS and OPEN_MHEALTH
sub_elements.quality_note: Four media types with MIME types plus the underlying data standards on every file collection. The four FAIRhub media types do not themselves cover the WFDB waveform files, which the file_collections entries supply instead.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: four typed entries; external_resources: docs.aireadi.org with a description of what each documentation section covers, plus aireadi.org, the team, data-sharing and contact pages, the Zenodo community, the AI-READI GitHub organization and the CDS v0.1.1 specification, with restrictions (CC-BY 4.0) and a future_guarantees statement
sub_elements.quality_note: Both slots populated with resolvable targets, and the documentation entry states what a reader gains from each resource rather than listing bare links.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: distribution_formats lists six entries with FAIRhub access_urls; page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 is an accessible landing page; license_and_use_terms grants a licence to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works, so the datasets-shared condition is met
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms: 'grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works ... tailored to enable reuse of the AI-READI dataset for commercial or research purposes'; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research
sub_elements.quality_note: Reuse is permitted for commercial and research purposes with the permitted and restricted acts spelled out. Sharing is limited to other licensees on identical terms, which is a real constraint the record states plainly rather than eliding.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence: populated distribution_formats with media types and accessible FAIRhub URLs
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to names WFDB for ECG, OMOP CDM for clinical data with one CSV per CDM table, NASA ESDS guidelines for environmental data, DICOM for all retinal imaging and Open mHealth for wearable data; conforms_to_standard lists CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, RO_CRATE; distribution_formats carries MIME types
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality is mapped to a named community format standard and each file collection repeats its own standards. Character encoding is not stated for any format, the one gap against the sub-element's wording.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: Clinical Dataset Structure (CDS) v0.1.1 with per-datatype format standards, plus an RO-Crate metadata file conforming to RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT and FAIRscape profile 0.1; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; instances[0].data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels: the dataset layout specification with a version, the per-directory format standards, and the metadata schema this record itself conforms to.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence
sub_elements.evidence: variables: nine entries (HbA1c, continuous blood glucose, best-corrected visual acuity logMAR, letter contrast sensitivity, MoCA total score, systolic blood pressure, step count, PM2.5) each with data_type, unit where applicable, measurement_technique naming the instrument and protocol, and quality_notes; a tenth entry marks the list as a representative subset and points to https://docs.aireadi.org
sub_elements.quality_note: Variable-level metadata is rich and actionable: instrument, sampling rate, viewing distance, reference range and scoring rules are given. Two real gaps: no variable carries an ontology or dictionary identifier, and the tenth entry is a scope note occupying a variable row rather than a variable. The record discloses the subset scope rather than implying coverage.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: two categories with examples and usage_notes covering the verified-ID access condition and the model-distribution and third-party-model conditions; prohibited_uses: six entries covering clinical treatment decisions, re-identification, sharing with model vendors, onward transfer, reproduction in publications beyond five figures, and watermark removal
sub_elements.quality_note: Guidance is operative and specific enough to act on, including the memorisation-minimisation obligation before releasing a trained model. discouraged_uses is absent, but intended and prohibited uses together answer the sub-element.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: description (E1) states the dataset was collected from 2,280 adults with and without type 2 diabetes across three named clinical sites; keywords (E1) include Diabetes mellitus and Eye exam; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes EHR screening, REDCap recruitment and in-person study visits; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted' and hipaa_compliant 'compliant' (E2) indicate governance constraints
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews[0]: University of Washington IRB, protocol STUDY00016228, initial approval 20 December 2022, approval letter published with the documentation, annual renewal due within 90 days of expiration, reliance agreements with UAB and UCSD; ethical_reviews[1]: RO-Crate ethical review by Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans; ethical_reviews[2]: Native Biodata Consortium engagement; human_subject_research.ethics_review_board gives the Human Subjects Division address and hsdrely@uw.edu; regulatory_compliance records NCT06002048 and the not-FDA-regulated status
sub_elements.quality_note: IRB documentation is specific and consistent with involves_human_subjects true, and the record distinguishes the dataset's own ethics review from the prospective tribal-data governance engagement. No data_protection_impacts slot is present at all, so the DPIA question is left unanswered rather than answered in the negative. The reviewing body's institutional name conflict (RO-Crate 'Washington University IRB' against a uw.edu address) is flagged in source_caveats and resolved in favour of the University of Washington reading.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same E1/E2/E8 evidence: 2,280 human participants in the description, clinical recruitment in collection_mechanisms, restricted confidentiality level in E2
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; method: 'No identifiers were collected, so no active de-identification was necessary ... The public set is stripped of Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule using the Safe Harbor method', with FAIRhub's 'NoDeIdentification' type code recorded alongside the flags for direct identifier removal and HIPAA de-identification applied and date shifting and k-anonymization not applied; identifiers_removed lists PHI, sex, race/ethnicity and medications
sub_elements.quality_note: A named method appropriate to health data, with the removed elements enumerated and the apparent contradiction between the FAIRhub type code and the Safe Harbor account explained rather than left standing. The source_caveat records that the healthsheet's own re-identification and de-identification items came back empty, so the account is assembled from other sources.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same E1/E2/E8 evidence
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.reidentification_risk: 'a theoretical risk of future re-identification ... AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level identification'; privacy_techniques: dissemination system, strict licence, static licensee watermarking, devices chosen without video, audio, GPS or phone syncing, encrypted servers under Level 3 data security classification; data_linkage names the controlled-access variables; future_use_impacts repeats the risk and the mitigations
sub_elements.quality_note: The risk is assessed rather than asserted absent, and each protection is tied to the risk it addresses, including the device-selection reasoning, which is a substantive privacy-by-design claim.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same E1/E2/E8 evidence
sub_elements.evidence: informed_consent[0].consent_obtained: true; consent_type: written, electronically in REDCap via a unique emailed code or in person, with FAIRhub's registry code 'ConsentSpecifiedNotElsewhereCategorised'; consent_scope limits the public version to type 2 diabetes research and records that consent is not non-commercial-only, not geographically restricted and does not prohibit methods development; consent_documentation names the approved form (AI-READI Consent Form, Standard, Mod 17 May 2023) and the UCSD Experimental Subject's Bill of Rights; withdrawal_mechanism plus collection_consents, consent_revocations and collection_notifications
sub_elements.quality_note: Consent is documented end to end: how it was obtained, what it permits, which form was used at which site, how participants were notified, and that data already shared stays in the dataset after withdrawal. That last limitation is stated rather than glossed.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same E1/E2/E8 evidence
sub_elements.evidence: at_risk_populations.special_protections: minors excluded (40 to 85 eligibility), pregnancy and gestational diabetes as exclusions, rideshare and parking/transit cost coverage for participants with transport barriers; participant_compensation: 200 US dollars for the study visit funded through the grant, paid when data and devices are returned, not prorated, with the note that transport costs above 25 US dollars are not reimbursed
sub_elements.quality_note: Compensation amount, mechanism, timing and its limits are all recorded. The at_risk_groups_included boolean is deliberately omitted with a source_caveat explaining that the IRB application's protected-populations checkboxes were unfilled, which is the honest treatment of an unanswered source.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations[0].subpopulation_elements_present: false with the reason (sex, race and ethnicity are held under controlled access); distribution gives cohort counts by race/ethnicity (Hispanic 380, Asian 545, Black 519, white 836), sex (male 951, female 1,329), diabetes status (776/560/686/258) and mean age 60.8 +/- 11.3; human_subject_research.special_populations gives the 40-85 eligibility and the pregnancy, gestational and type 1 exclusions
sub_elements.quality_note: The boolean and the aggregates are reconciled explicitly: cohort-level counts are published while per-instance labels are not, which is why the flag reads false. All three aggregate axes sum to 2,280.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: instances[0].counts: 2280; total_file_count: 356343; total_size_bytes: 3815969779678; splits: 1,576 training, 352 validation, 352 testing at 70/15/15; subsets carry is_data_split and is_subpopulation flags; file_collections give per-directory file counts
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts are given at participant, file, byte, split and directory level, and they reconcile: the split sizes sum to 2,280 and the directory counts to 356,334 with the nine root metadata files accounting for the remainder.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: is_tabular: false; variables carries nine described variables with data_type, unit, measurement_technique and quality_notes; instances[0].notes states the release spans tabular, imaging and physiological waveform data with no unstructured text
sub_elements.quality_note: The tabular flag is correct for a multimodal release and is explained rather than left bare. The variable list is a declared representative subset, with the full dictionary deferred to docs.aireadi.org and the OMOP CDM mapping.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances[0].instance_type: Individual study participant, data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:43, label: false, with notes enumerating survey, clinical, retinal imaging, environmental sensor, CGM and wearable activity data per instance; keywords name Diabetes mellitus, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring and Retinal imaging
sub_elements.quality_note: The condition and the modalities are both recorded, with an ontology term for the topic. The record explains why data_substrate is omitted (no single B2AI substrate term covers a multimodal instance) instead of approximating it.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: seven entries covering skipped survey questions, wearable battery and malfunction gaps, imaging noise and cooperation, device returns with lost data, Optomed undilated image variability, Heidelberg Spectralis operator dependence and FLIO's light exposure and 1 cm movement tolerance; missing_data_documentation gives patterns, causes and handling_strategy; sampling_strategies records non-probability wave-based recruitment
sub_elements.quality_note: Anomalies are device- and modality-specific rather than generic, and missingness is characterised structurally (whole study elements or whole device datasets rather than scattered fields) with the fill rule and the site-PI approval requirement stated.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated with FAIRhub access_urls and a licence permitting reuse
sub_elements.evidence: version: 3.0.0; issued: 2025-11-17T00:00:00Z; status: published
sub_elements.quality_note: Semantic version tied to a release date and to its own DOI.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; versions_available lists all three releases with DOI, date, participant count and size, and records that version 2.0.0 is no longer accessible on FAIRhub; version_details describes the version dropdown at docs.aireadi.org and the separate healthsheets at /docs/1/ and /docs/2/
sub_elements.quality_note: Each version is addressable by its own DOI and documentation set, and the record states plainly which version is no longer retrievable rather than implying all three remain available.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.version_details: added participants, retained largely the same fields, dropped the Snellen visual acuity variables in favour of logMAR only, added one imaging device in year 2 and three in year 3, moved from ad hoc to automated plus custom processing, and introduced the recommended split; updates.update_details points at the CHANGELOG file and docs.aireadi.org; known_limitations records the Snellen drop as a methodological limitation
sub_elements.quality_note: Changes between versions are described at the level of specific variables and devices, not as a pointer to a changelog alone. No errata slot is present, and no correction to a released version is recorded.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: 'Approximately once a year'; update_details: the dataset itself will not be updated, new versions will be released with additional instances as participants complete visits, enrollment is ongoing; retention_limit records no retention limit and that older versions are superseded rather than updated
sub_elements.quality_note: The maintenance model is stated explicitly as static versioned releases rather than in-place updates, which matters for anyone pinning a version. The observed cadence (May 2024, November 2024, November 2025) is not exactly annual, but the record reports the stated plan.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: nine entries with source_description, source_type, raw_data_format (.fda, .sdt, DICOM, .xml, .FIT, .csv) and access_details; raw_sources records that raw data are retained by the project, not shared, because they are unmapped and may contain PHI in free text; preprocessing_strategies traces each device export to its released standard format
sub_elements.quality_note: The chain from device export to released file is traceable per modality, and the reason raw data are withheld is given rather than left as a bare refusal. No was_derived_from or release_notes slot, but the derivation is documented in substance.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: enabling AI/ML research into type 2 diabetes including salutogenic pathways; creating a model and blueprint for ethically sourced FAIR datasets; increasing access to AI/ML research through recruitment and training. addressing_gaps names the lack of large inclusive multimodal datasets, the lack of AI-ready diverse datasets, and the documented under-representation in a 2000-2020 meta-epidemiological review
sub_elements.quality_note: Purpose and the specific research gap are separated and both are concrete, with the diversity gap supported by a named literature finding rather than asserted.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: downstream pseudotime manifold analysis to predict disease trajectories across severity strata; reconstruction of a temporal atlas of type 2 diabetes development and reversal; general multimodal AI/ML model development across the named modalities
sub_elements.quality_note: Named analytic methods rather than generic 'machine learning', and they connect to the recruitment design (balance across four severity categories) that the composition slots describe.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: National Institutes of Health (NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program), Research to Prevent Blindness, Microsoft AI for Good Lab (cloud services), and device manufacturers providing in-kind contributions (Topcon, Optomed, iCare World, Carl Zeiss loans; Heidelberg Engineering, Dexcom, Garmin discounts)
sub_elements.quality_note: Four funders with the mechanism stated for each, including in-kind and cloud support that a narrower reading would have dropped.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: funders[0].grants[0]: 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project (award number OT2OD032644)' with the NIH RePORTER project-details URL as the id; notes give the original award record (application ID 10471118, project number 1OT2OD032644-01, FY2022, University of Washington awardee, award amount 5,026,499 US dollars, period 2022-09-01 to 2025-08-31) and additional support P30DK035816 and UL1TR003096
sub_elements.quality_note: OT2OD032644 matches the NIH pattern (activity code OT2, institute OD, serial), and the record explains that two RePORTER records exist for the same core project number and which one the identifier points at. The supplementary awards are also well formed.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: AI-READI Consortium as organizational creator, principal_investigator Aaron Lee (ORCID:0000-0002-7452-1648), with the institutional collaborators from FAIRhub study metadata (NIH, California Medical Innovations Institute, Johns Hopkins, OHSU, Stanford, UAB, UCSD); maintainers gives the maintaining team, hosting and contact@aireadi.org; data_collectors describes site coordinators and consortium roles
sub_elements.quality_note: Creator, maintainer, collector and funder acknowledgement are all recorded with contact routes. The record flags in a creators-level source_caveat that the PI's institutional affiliation differs between two tier-1 sources.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection is identified elsewhere (acquisition_methods and collection_timeframes populated, direct_collection.is_direct true) and the datasets-shared condition is met via distribution_formats and the FAIRhub access URLs
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: twelve entries naming REDCap for questionnaires and clinical data, EHR screening with ICD-10 codes R73.09 and E11.X, the Philips PageWriter TC30 with recorded chair angle, Optomed Aurora IQ and iCare Eidon fundus imaging with field of view and dilation status, four OCT/OCTA platforms with named scan protocols, Heidelberg FLIO with its two wavelength channels, Dexcom G6 at 5-minute intervals over 10 days, Garmin Vivosmart 5 at 5-second sampling, the LeeLab Anura sensor, the vision instruments, monofilament and MoCA testing, and the blood and urine collection and shipping route
sub_elements.quality_note: This is replication-grade detail: instrument, setting, duration, sampling rate and protocol variant are given per modality, along with the biorepository destination and the laboratory that ran which assays.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same evidence: collection identified and datasets shared
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: was_directly_observed true, was_reported_by_subjects true, was_inferred_derived false, was_validated_verified true, with details on the domain split and the medication cross-referencing verification, and the RO-Crate collection type of manual human curation; raw_data_sources gives nine sources with device-native formats
sub_elements.quality_note: The booleans are each supported by a stated example, and the record notes that the healthsheet answer covers only observed and reported acquisition, so was_inferred_derived false reflects the source rather than an assumption.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: external_resources (E10) names 'the GitHub organization of the AI-READI project at https://github.com/AI-READI'; purposes (E7) state the project aims to establish standards, best practices and guidelines for the collection, preparation and sharing of data for AI/ML, so the software-output condition is met
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: mapping to OMOP CDM and DICOM, conversion of Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt to DICOM and Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, WFDB storage for ECG, Safe Harbor stripping of PHI plus sex/race/medications, and the CDS v0.1.1 directory layout with per-datatype manifest.tsv; cleaning_strategies: REDCap range flagging with coordinator and data manager review, checks for skip-pattern flow, fillable missingness, omission and duplication, edits only under site PI approval, then central QC and a published dqd_omop.json supporting the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard's 3,500-plus checks
sub_elements.quality_note: Preprocessing and cleaning are both documented as pipelines with decision rules and an auditable quality artefact shipped with the data. Labelling is answered by an explicit negative (instances[0].label false; the description states no annotation or labeling was performed so the release stays hypothesis-agnostic), which is the correct answer here rather than a gap. No imputation_protocols slot, though missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states the fill rule.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same condition: the AI-READI GitHub organization is referenced in external_resources (E10) and standards/best-practice production is a stated purpose (E7)
sub_elements.evidence: No software_and_tools slot exists in the record. Tools appear only incidentally inside other slots: REDCap (collection_mechanisms), the MoCA Duo application (collection_mechanisms), the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard and dqd_omop.json (cleaning_strategies), and a bare organization URL https://github.com/AI-READI (external_resources)
sub_elements.quality_note: Fails the sub-element. The conversion tooling that preprocessing_strategies relies on (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth, ECG to WFDB) is never named, no version is given for any tool, and no repository is identified under the GitHub organization, so the processing steps cannot be reproduced from this record.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met via distribution_formats and the FAIRhub access URLs
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: docs.aireadi.org with per-section content described, aireadi.org and its team, data-sharing and contact pages, the AI-READI Zenodo community, the GitHub organization and the CDS v0.1.1 specification at cds-specification.readthedocs.io; conforms_to and conforms_to_standard name CDS, WFDB, OMOP CDM, NASA ESDS, DICOM, Open mHealth, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT and FAIRscape profile 0.1; related_datasets carries the Nature Metabolism comment and the BMJ Open protocol DOIs
sub_elements.quality_note: Standards are named with versions where the bundle gives them, and the documentation entry records its own licence (CC-BY 4.0) and a candid statement that no persistence guarantee is available for the documentation site.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: six typed entries covering representativeness (urban, hospital-based, no Pacific Islander or Native American participants), coverage (pilot and interim releases not balanced), scope (public release omits PHI, sex, race/ethnicity and medications; raw data withheld), temporal (cross-sectional, one visit per participant), scope (40-85 eligibility, English requirement, pregnancy and type 1 exclusions) and methodological (Snellen variables dropped in 3.0.0), several with scope_impact or recommended_mitigation
sub_elements.quality_note: Limitations are typed, specific and each states what it constrains, including a mitigation pointing to the recommended splits. The English-language requirement is connected to its recruitment consequence rather than listed as a bare criterion.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: selection_bias (volunteer bias) with wave-based composition adjustment; sampling_bias (EHR screening of three academic health systems, urban hospital-based) with uniform protocols and geographic site selection; representation_bias with affected_subsets naming the four race/ethnicity and four diabetes severity groups and a five-part mitigation; measurement_bias (multiple device models per measure, operator-dependent image quality) with device documentation for repeatability. future_use_impacts records the anticipated-harm assessment and the re-identification risk
sub_elements.quality_note: Four distinct enum bias types, each with a description, a mitigation and, for representation bias, the affected subsets. future_use_impacts supplies the downstream social-impact statement the sub-element asks for.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: seven entries including survey non-response, Garmin charging gaps every two to three days, imaging noise and participant cooperation, devices returned with lost data, data collisions, Optomed undilated image variability within and between participants, Heidelberg Spectralis operator dependence leading to skipped modalities, and FLIO's light discomfort and 1 cm movement tolerance
sub_elements.quality_note: Anomalies are attributed to specific devices and procedures with the mechanism that causes them, which lets a user anticipate where the data will be thin.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements[0]: public dataset contains no sensitive data, with the controlled-access variables enumerated (race/ethnicity, 5-digit zip, motor vehicle accident reports, sex, genetic sequencing, past health records, medications); sensitive_elements[1]: the RO-Crate's rai:personalSensitiveInformation categories; confidential_elements records no confidential or personally identifiable content; participant_privacy.data_linkage repeats the controlled-access linkage
sub_elements.quality_note: Sensitive content is enumerated for both tiers and the disagreement between the two sources is analysed rather than averaged, with the governing reading named. The cost is that the two entries carry opposite sensitive_elements_present booleans, which a machine reading the flag alone cannot resolve. No content_warnings slot, which is defensible for this data type.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: three entries covering the University of Washington IRB with protocol id, approval date, renewal cycle and reliance agreements; the four named RO-Crate ethical reviewers with Camille Nebeker as contact_person and a note explaining why no organization is recorded; and the Native Biodata Consortium engagement with a note that no Native American cohort data are in version 3.0.0
sub_elements.quality_note: Review documentation is thorough and each entry states the limits of what the bundle supports. No explicit conflict-of-interest declaration is made; the device manufacturer loans and discounts are disclosed under funders but never framed as a conflict, and no patent or commercialisation position is stated.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition met: distribution_formats populated with FAIRhub access_urls and a licence permitting reuse
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://fairhub.io/; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; maintainers record hosting on FAIRhub through Microsoft Azure; use_repository gives the FAIRhub dataset page with a view count of 24,636 and a citation count of 0
sub_elements.quality_note: FAIRhub is a recognised research data platform, and the record adds the hosting arrangement and the platform's own usage panel rather than only naming the publisher.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publications are identified: citation names the RO-Crate associatedPublication form, and related_datasets carries doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x (Nature Metabolism) and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449 (BMJ Open); the datasets-shared condition is also met
sub_elements.evidence: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3', followed by the statement that the operative requirement is the citation instructions at https://docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/citation; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete citation string with version and DOI, and the record distinguishes the form it recorded from the operative citation policy the licence imposes rather than presenting its own string as authoritative.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, RO_CRATE; conforms_to describes CDS v0.1.1, the one-to-one OMOP CDM table mapping, NASA ESDS guidelines and the RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT plus FAIRscape profile 0.1 metadata file; every file_collections entry repeats its own conforms_to_standard list
sub_elements.quality_note: Seven community standards, versioned where the bundle gives versions, and asserted per directory as well as at the dataset level so a consumer knows which standard governs which files.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources[0] describes docs.aireadi.org section by section (citation requirements, access and training prerequisites, mini-subset, Azure Storage access, healthsheet, per-domain clinical context and variables, AI-readiness and FAIR considerations, controlled variables, changelog) under CC-BY 4.0; external_resources[1] gives the project site, team page, data-sharing goals page, contact page, Zenodo community, GitHub organization and the CDS specification; notes describe the year-long research internship programme with its 2023-2024 cohort composition
sub_elements.quality_note: Documentation is not just linked but characterised, and the training programme is recorded, which is the outreach dimension of this sub-element.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets-shared evidence
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 with participant counts, sizes and the note that 2.0.0 is no longer accessible; is_described_by doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449 with full bibliographic detail
sub_elements.quality_note: Four relationships, each typed and each target resolvable by DOI. The two is_described_by targets are journal articles in a dataset-typed slot, which the record discloses in each description and justifies as the relationship the bundle attests.

strengths: Numerical claims reconcile against each other and against the record's own structures: split sizes sum to 2,280, all three cohort aggregate axes sum to 2,280, and the two arithmetic caveats the record raises (nine root metadata files, a 419,614-byte shortfall) are exactly reproducible from the nine file_collections entries

Collection protocol is replication-grade, naming every instrument with its settings: chair angle for the ECG, dilation status and field of view per fundus camera, named scan protocols for four OCT platforms, wavelength channels for FLIO, and sampling intervals for the CGM, wearable and environmental sensors

Ethics documentation is complete and internally consistent: IRB protocol id, approval date, renewal cycle and reliance agreements, the named consent form and site variations, the withdrawal mechanism together with its stated limit, compensation amount, timing and reimbursement cap, and a re-identification risk assessment tied to specific mitigations

Eleven source disagreements are enumerated at the record root and repeated on the affected slots, each naming the sources, their rank and whether one was preferred or both recorded, which makes every contested value auditable rather than silently merged

Derived values are labelled as derived: confidentiality_level and hipaa_compliant both carry caveats stating that no source uses those words, and unmappable source terms (the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)') are preserved in prose rather than forced into an enum
weaknesses: No software_and_tools slot; the .fda/.sdt to DICOM and .FIT to Open mHealth conversion tooling and the central team's processing steps are unnamed and unversioned, and the GitHub reference is an organization URL with no repository
sensitive_elements carries two entries with opposite sensitive_elements_present booleans, so the structured flag contradicts itself even though the prose explains which reading governs
The institutional attribution conflict is disclosed but unresolved: governance sits with Washington University in St. Louis while IRB oversight and the NIH award sit with the University of Washington
No data_protection_impacts slot at all, and no conflict-of-interest statement despite device manufacturer loans and discounts on the very instruments used for measurement
Variables carry no ontology or dictionary identifiers, no character encoding is stated for any format, and the variables list ends with a scope note occupying a variable row
recommendations: Add software_and_tools entries naming the format-conversion and curation tools with versions and the specific AI-READI repositories, and record the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard with its version
Collapse sensitive_elements to one entry carrying the governing boolean for the released data, and move the RO-Crate data-source categories to a note so the flag is unambiguous
State which institution is authoritative for data governance as distinct from IRB oversight, keeping the alternative as a recorded source position
Add data_protection_impacts, stating explicitly if no assessment was conducted, and add a conflict-of-interest declaration to ethical_reviews covering the device manufacturer in-kind contributions

Add LOINC or OMOP concept identifiers to the variables that have them, state the character encoding of the CSV, JSON and Markdown distributions, and move the representative-subset scope note out of the variables list
